The Free plan offers unlimited sending.

Broadcasts, Automations, dedicated IPs, security credentials, or a broad integration list.

Resend is a separate provider, not a change to the auth platform's own limiter: the platform's dashboard rate limit still has to be raised by hand after wiring SMTP, and Resend's own free tier reimposes a 100-emails-a-day cap.

emails.next_step_value: Create an account, then use a verified domain and API key to try an API flow in test mode without sending to real recipients.

events.subject: Resend for transactional product email
events.preview_text: Set up one event-driven message and inspect the API flow in test mode.
events.body:
Resend is available for developers to send transactional product email through an API. Start with one event-driven message, such as a signup confirmation or password reset.

Create an account, verify your domain, and generate an API key. Resend’s test mode lets you simulate email events and inspect the API flow without sending test messages to real recipients.

That gives you a concrete sending route to evaluate before relying on it in a live signup flow. An API test shows you how this flow works. Production delivery and a hosted auth platform’s SMTP setup require separate checks.

Get started

events.message: Email 1, draft 1: "Supabase Auth logs and SMTP setup"
events.subject: Supabase Auth logs and SMTP setup
events.preview_text: See the sender configuration and the separate Auth limit to check.
events.body:
Checking Supabase Auth logs can help diagnose a 429 on signup or OTP email. It still leaves the SMTP sender and Auth rate limit to configure separately.

Resend is available as an email sending platform for developers to send transactional product email through SMTP, an API, or SDKs. If you use Supabase Auth, our guide shows where to enter Resend’s SMTP credentials in your project’s Authentication settings.

Changing the sender alone does not remove Supabase’s Auth rate limit. After custom SMTP is saved, Supabase initially limits Auth email to 30 messages per hour. Check its Rate Limits settings against your intended volume.

The guide shows the configuration path so you can decide whether it applies to your Supabase Auth project.
events.call_to_action: Read the Supabase SMTP setup guide
